_strings.@@32c5e4d3f884: Treaty conformity — MD does NOT conform to federal tax treaties: income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is STILL taxable by MD. Do not carry a federal treaty exclusion onto the state return. (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state's Internal Revenue Code conformity date and its deduction/credit conformity are separate questions; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Maryland Form 502 starts from federal adjusted gross income (line 1 = "Adjusted gross income from your federal return"), so treaty-exempt income is initially excluded — BUT Maryland then adds it back. Instruction 12 (Additions to Income), Line 5 "Other Additions to Income," code letter g reads verbatim: "Income exempt from federal tax by federal law or treaty that is not exempt from Maryland tax." This is an explicit add-back of federally treaty-exempt income (analogous to California's Schedule CA addback), entered on Form 502 line 5 with code letter g. Therefore treaty-exempt income IS re-taxed by Maryland and the state does NOT conform. Source: 2023 Resident Booklet, Instruction 12, code letter g (marylandcomptroller.gov / marylandtaxes.gov).

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form 502 line 21: 'Maryland tax (from Tax Table or Computation Worksheet Schedules I or II)' This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply Form 502 line 20 'Taxable net income (Subtract line 19 from line 18.)'. Compute it on the form: line 1 federal AGI + additions (lines 2-6) - subtractions (lines 8-15) = line 16 Maryland adjusted gross income; minus line 17 deduction (standard = 15% of line 16 clamped to $1,700-$2,550 for filing statuses 1/3/6 or $3,450-$5,150 for statuses 2/4/5 via Worksheet 16A, OR itemized = federal itemized deductions less state and local income taxes) = line 18 net income; minus line 19 exemption amount (Exemption Amount Chart 10A: $3,200 per person phased down by federal AGI, +$1,000 each age-65/blind) = line 20. Because Maryland's standard deduction is a percentage of income with min/max clamps and its exemptions phase out by federal AGI, neither is shipped as a fixed amount — the caller must supply line 20 with deductions and exemptions already taken on the form. Tax-table mandate below $100,000: Instruction 17 states 'You must use the tax tables if your taxable income is less than $100,000' and 'The 2023 Maryland tax rate schedules are shown so you can see the tax rate that applies to all levels of income; however, do not use them to figure your tax.' Bracket math may differ by a few dollars within the $50 table bands (e.g. schedule math at exactly $50,000 single gives $2,322.50 while the table band value differs slightly); the filed Form 502 must use the 2023 Maryland Tax Table for line-20 income under $100,000 and Worksheet Schedules 17A at $100,000 or more. Mandatory LOCAL income tax is NOT modeled: every Maryland county and Baltimore City levies a local income tax on the SAME Form 502 line-20 taxable net income, entered on Form 502 line 28. 2023 Local Tax Rate Chart (Instruction 19) rates run from .0225 (Worcester County; also the nonresident rate) to .0320 (e.g. Baltimore City, Baltimore, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's); Anne Arundel County is graduated for 2023 (.0270 on taxable income of $1-$50,000, .0281 on the excess over $50,000 — use the Anne Arundel tax table/Worksheet 19D) and Frederick County is .0275 or .0296 depending on filing status and income. Local tax adds roughly 2.25%-3.20% of line-20 income on top of the state tax computed here. Standard deduction is NOT shipped because it is income-dependent: 15% of Maryland adjusted gross income (Form 502 line 16) with a minimum of $1,700 and maximum of $2,550 for filing statuses 1, 3, 6 (single, married filing separately, dependent taxpayer) and a minimum of $3,450 and maximum of $5,150 for statuses 2, 4, 5 (joint, head of household, qualifying surviving spouse) — Standard Deduction Worksheet 16A, Instruction 16. Itemizers instead enter federal itemized deductions less state and local income taxes (lines 17a/17b). Take the deduction on Form 502 line 17 before supplying line 20 as the base. Personal and dependent exemptions are NOT shipped because they phase out by federal AGI (Exemption Amount Chart 10A, Instruction 10): $3,200 each for taxpayer, spouse, and each dependent when federal AGI is $100,000 or less, reduced to $1,600 (FAGI $100,000-$125,000), $800 ($125,000-$150,000), and $0 (over $150,000) for single/MFS, and to $1,600 ($150,000-$175,000), $800 ($175,000-$200,000), and $0 (over $200,000) for joint/HoH/QSS; dependent taxpayers (filing status 6) get $0 for themselves. An additional $1,000 each for age 65-or-over and/or blind (taxpayer and spouse) is never phased out. These are genuine base reductions subtracted on Form 502 line 19 BEFORE the rate applies — they are already inside the caller-supplied line-20 base. Filing-status mapping: Maryland prints exactly two schedules. Tax Rate Schedule I covers Single, Married Filing Separately, and Dependent Taxpayers (and fiduciaries); Tax Rate Schedule II covers Joint, Head of Household, and Qualifying Surviving Spouse. Qualifying surviving spouse therefore maps to married_filing_jointly with no difference; a dependent taxpayer (filing status 6) uses the shipped 'single' brackets. The printed '$X plus Y% of excess over $Z' constants in both 2023 schedules equal the exact cumulative sum of the prior brackets (verified: Schedule I $90.00/$4,697.50/$5,947.50/$7,260.00/$12,760.00; Schedule II $90.00/$7,072.50/$8,322.50/$10,947.50/$15,072.50) — no rounding divergence, so marginal bracket math reproduces the worksheet exactly. Items after line 21 are NOT modeled: line 21a recaptured credit (Form 502CR Part DD) is added, and lines 22-26 CREDITS are subtracted from tax — Maryland earned income credit (50% of federal EIC, line 22, plus a refundable portion up to 45% of federal EIC on line 42), poverty level credit (line 23), and Form 502CR credits (line 24). These are tax CREDITS, not income exemptions, and must never be treated as base reductions. This pack models the resident Form 502 only. Nonresidents file Form 505/505NR and pay a special nonresident tax (the local-rate chart lists 'Nonresidents use .0225') in lieu of the county local tax; part-year residents must prorate exemptions and deductions under Instruction 26.
